name: Factory Method
intent: Let subclasses decide which concrete object to create, while shared code works with the abstract type.
scenario: A delivery app plans shipments. Road delivery uses trucks, sea delivery uses ships. The planning code should not care which.
problem: Your planning code needs a transport object, but which one depends on the kind of delivery. Writing new Truck() or new Ship() inside the planner ties it to every concrete class, and every new vehicle means editing it.
solution: Move creation into one overridable method, the factory method. The base class calls createTransport() inside its planning logic. Each subclass overrides it to return its own product. The planner only ever sees the Transport interface.
pain: planDelivery() contains an if/else that knows Truck and Ship
Adding air delivery means editing that function (and every copy of the switch)
The planner cannot be tested without real transports
Choosing the transport and using it are tangled together
benefits: planDelivery() only knows the Transport interface
Air delivery is a new subclass, with no edits to existing code
Tests can subclass and return a fake transport
whenToUse: A class cannot know in advance which concrete type it will need
You want subclasses or configuration to choose the type, not the caller
You want a clear extension point for adding new product types
whenNotToUse: There is only one product type and no sign of more: use new directly
A plain function that returns the right object is enough (a simple factory function)
Adding a subclass per variant is heavier than the problem deserves
pitfalls: Subclass explosion: one creator class per product can pile up quickly
People call this pattern Simple Factory or static factory; those are different and simpler
The base class method name must be documented as an extension point, or nobody knows to override it
Returning an unrelated type breaks the contract the planner relies on

quiz.question: An exporter class has code that says: if format is pdf then new PdfWriter, else if csv then new CsvWriter. Product asks for xlsx, then json. Each time someone must edit the exporter and re-test it. Which change fixes the cause?
options: Add the xlsx and json branches, and move the if chain into a helper so the exporter file stays short
Make writer creation an overridable method, so each exporter subclass returns its own writer type
Make PdfWriter and CsvWriter singletons so that the exporter never has to create them itself
Pass the format string deeper into each writer so that the writer decides what it should write
quiz.explanation: The exporter's shared logic should only know the writer interface. Putting creation in an overridable method means a new format is a new subclass with no edits to the old code. Moving the if chain to a helper keeps the same switch, it only moves it.

quiz.question: A team has one Logger class created in one place, and no other logger type is planned. A reviewer suggests an abstract LoggerCreator with a concrete creator subclass for the only logger. What is the best call?
options: Create the logger directly and add the factory method when a second type actually appears
Add the creator hierarchy now, since it is cheaper than refactoring once the code is in production
Add it now, but only with an abstract creator, to avoid the cost of the concrete subclass
Use a static global variable for the logger, as creating it in more than one place is the real risk
quiz.explanation: With one product and no sign of more, a factory method adds classes and indirection for nothing. It is easy to introduce later when a second variant shows up. A global variable adds hidden shared state and solves a different problem. Adding the abstract creator now still adds indirection with no second product.

quiz.question: A system has 15 creator subclasses. Each one only overrides createHandler to return a different handler class, and none of them has other logic. They are all picked by a config value. What is the better design?
options: Make each handler a singleton so that the 15 creator subclasses are no longer needed
Use one creator that takes a handler constructor from a registry keyed by the config value
Keep the 15 subclasses, because replacing them breaks the open/closed principle
Move all 15 createHandler methods into one base class and select with a type code
quiz.explanation: When the subclasses differ only in what they return, a registry of constructors gives the same extension point without 15 classes. A new handler is one registry entry. The factory method pays off when each creator also carries its own logic, and a base class with a type code is a switch again.
